messages:
Dave_support: FYI getting an escalation from Acme — they see p99 latency ~1.2s on /v1/generate since ~09:10 UTC, says customers timing out. Weird: our alerting didn't fire until they pinged support.
Anna_SRE: ouch. which dashboard/metric are they looking at?
Mike_Observability: they sent screenshots — Datadog panel (per-route p95) shows ~320ms at 09:05, then Grafana p99 panel shows 1.2s at 09:12.
Carol_Product: we rolled a runtime config at 08:50 (kernel-selector bump) but it was low-risk. rolling back now would be painful. can we validate metric sources first?
Dave_support: they ALSO included request ids: req_9f3b... attached ingress logs.
infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary deploy at 08:49: deploy/infra-runtime v2.14 -> canary -> promoted @09:20
Anna_SRE: timeline: deploy 08:49, canary promoted 09:20, customer saw p99 spike ~09:10. that suggests canary behavior or rollout mix.
Mike_Observability: quick note: the two panels are not comparable. Datadog shows agent-side digest quantiles averaged across hosts. Grafana uses Prometheus histogram_quantile on summed buckets — rollup quantiles != quantile(histograms).
Anna_SRE: classic mismatch. what PromQL is Grafana using?
Mike_Observability: Grafana query:

  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

Datadog uses 1m agent-side digest quantiles aggregated per-host.
Carol_Product: so Datadog smooths spikes; Prometheus derived p99 can amplify when buckets differ or scrapes gap.
Dave_support: customer insists our API degraded. we need repro/answer + immediate mitigation.
Anna_SRE: triage steps (quick):
- check raw request latencies for the provided request ids
- check host-level distribution (which hosts show tail)
- sanity-check exporter scrape windows and any bucket config drift
- confirm aggregation window (1m vs 5m)

Mike_Observability: grep traces/logs for req_9f3b now.
Mike_Observability: found entries — host-12 has tailers around 09:08-09:11, host-19 looks normal.

logs snippet:

  host-12 | 2026-02-12T09:09:47Z | req_9f3b | duration_ms=1240 | route=/v1/generate | kernel-selector=fast_fp16
  host-12 | 2026-02-12T09:10:03Z | req_9f3b | duration_ms=1180 | sampling=0.02

Anna_SRE: that matches Grafana p99. so at least one host had genuine tail latency.
Dave_support: any recent config change on host-12?
Carol_Product: host-12 got the canary runtime patch; host-19 didn't. canary was small percent but some customers get pinned sockets.
Anna_SRE: pinned sessions can concentrate customer traffic on a canary host. also check kernel selector behavior — maybe fp16 path slower on long sequences.
Mike_Observability: prometheus exporter on host-12 had a scrape gap 09:06-09:09 — might bias rollups. also, we changed histogram bucket boundaries in exporter at 02:00 yesterday (widened buckets).
Anna_SRE: who changed exporter buckets?
Carol_Product: I merged a change to exporter max bucket le to 4s to reduce cardinality (#4321).
Mike_Observability: exact metric problem: Datadog agent computes per-host digest quantiles then averages; Prometheus sum(rate(bucket)) aggregates across hosts — if bucket le differ on one host aggregate is inconsistent. plus scrape gaps skew rates.
Anna_SRE: root causes: (A) a canary host (host-12) produced real tail latency; (B) metric aggregation inconsistency due to bucket change + scrape gaps leading to disagreement between Datadog and Grafana.
Anna_SRE: immediate mitigations we can do now:
- evict/drain host-12 from LB (fast, low-risk)
- throttle the canary rollout
- add a per-host p99 Grafana panel for triage
- add a short-term alert on host-12 tail > 800ms

Carol_Product: I'll drain host-12 now.

deploy-bot: LB drain initiated for host-12 by @Carol_Product

Carol_Product: host-12 drained and traffic rebalanced. monitoring: Datadog p95 stable; Grafana p99 dropped to ~350ms after the window moved.
Mike_Observability: dashboard fixes: we should make aggregation method explicit and show per-host breakdowns.
Anna_SRE: long-term fixes recommended:
- standardize histogram bucket boundaries across all exporters and ship centrally
- export a server-side HDR/histogram p99 metric (avoid cross-host quantile mixing)
- use recording rules for route_p99_ms with consistent windows and apply in dashboards/alerts
- add CI guard to prevent exporter bucket drift

Dave_support: please draft a short response for Acme we can send now.
Anna_SRE: draft for Acme (short): "We observed a transient tail on a canary host during a rollout and a mismatch between monitoring systems caused by differing aggregation methods. We drained the affected host and throttled the rollout. We're standardizing histogram buckets and adding a service-side p99 metric to prevent future confusion. We'll follow up once the fixes are in."
Carol_Product: grammar tweak and send.
Mike_Observability: action items created:
- Anna_SRE: add per-host p99 panels + note aggregation method (due EOD)
- Mike_Observability: standardize or revert exporter bucket change + add CI guard (48h)
- Carol_Product: pause further canary promotions until kernel-selector validated (done)
- Dave_support: send Acme draft + request logs (sent)

Anna_SRE: note for team: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...[5m])) by (le)) is only accurate when bucket boundaries are identical across all series. changing le on one exporter breaks aggregation; align or use server-side reporting.

deploy-bot: rollback requested for deploy/infra-runtime v2.14 by @Carol_Product — in progress

infra-bot: LB drain complete for host-12

Mike_Observability: I'll prototype HDR exporter to emit route_p99_ms from app-side, then we can use recording rules on stable metric.
Dave_support: customer: "thanks, we saw improvement after host drain. appreciate the transparency." :thumbsup: 

Anna_SRE: closing summary: root cause = transient canary tail on host-12 + metric aggregation inconsistency due to exporter bucket change and scrape gaps. mitigated by draining the host and halting rollout. next steps: standardize buckets, add service-side p99, fix dashboards and alerts. I'll open follow-ups in infra and observability repos and mark this thread resolved for now.
